definitions.explanation: A free-reed wind instrument with 17 bamboo pipes mounted on a small cup-shaped chamber, used in {雅楽|ががく} (Japanese court music). Produces an ethereal, sustained chord.

examples.japanese: ⟦{雅楽|ががく}→雅楽：27354_gagaku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{笙|しょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{独特|どくとく}→独特：01656_dokutoku⟧な⟦{和音|わおん}→和音：04751_waon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{奏|かな}でる→奏でる：12176_kanaderu⟧。
examples.english: In gagaku the sho produces distinctive sustained chords.

examples.japanese: {笙|しょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{音色|ねいろ}→音色：07422_neiro⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{天上|てんじょう}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{差|さ}し{込|こ}む→差し込む：04235_sashikomu⟧⟦{光|ひかり}→光：01707_hikari⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧たとえられる。
examples.english: The tone of the sho is likened to light streaming down from the heavens.

notes:
A traditional wind instrument central to ⟦{雅楽|ががく}→雅楽：27354_gagaku⟧ (Japanese court music). The 17 vertical bamboo pipes give it a distinctive shape resembling phoenix wings, and it is one of very few East Asian instruments that play chords. The player both inhales and exhales through the mouthpiece.

- {笙|しょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{吹|ふ}く→吹く：02445_fuku⟧: to play the sho

- {笙|しょう}⟦{奏者|そうしゃ}→奏者：06964_sousha⟧: sho player

- {篳篥|ひちりき}: hichiriki, double-reed instrument used alongside the sho in gagaku
- {龍笛|りゅうてき}: ryuteki, transverse flute used in gagaku
